label: Elmer Fudd
description: Vewy, vewy quiet, and hunting for your destination.
direction: Speak in Elmer Fudd's soft, lisping, sing-song voice with his famous w for r: hushed and sneaky, with little chuckles. Say navigation words such as turn, left, right, exit, distances, traffic and police clearly and normally.
notes: Voice model is a provisional pick from a Fish title search; find_voices.py auditions it and ship_roster.py build writes the final pick here. The w for r speech pattern lives only on the character words; navigation words (turn, left, right, exit, distances, arrived, traffic, police, camera) are spelled normally so a transcriber hears them. Turns and near distances stay plain.

rights.source_work: Elmer's Candid Camera (1940) and later Looney Tunes cartoons
rights.author: Warner Bros. Entertainment (character developed by Tex Avery, Bob Clampett and Chuck Jones)
rights.pd_basis: None. The character as Elmer dates from 1940 and remains under US copyright; the voice a clone would copy is a later performance, and Looney Tunes and the character's name are live Warner Bros. trademarks.
covered: The 43 lines of navigation dialogue below, which are original writing produced for this pack. A few greetings and alerts deliberately echo the character's well-known personality and catchphrases; those are the rights holder's, not ours.
not_covered: The character, which is not ours and is not in the public domain.
The character's name and the Looney Tunes name, which are live trademarks.
Any recorded voice performance of the character, by any performer.

The third-party voice model named in `voice`, which was uploaded by a member of the public and presented as a clone of that performance. No permission from the rights holder or the performer is claimed or implied.
Any commercial use. A platform's commercial-rights upsell cannot grant rights the uploader never held.
rights.notes: This preset is in copyright and says so. It is included because the pipeline should not pretend a rights position it does not have; see docs/presets.md before publishing anything built from it. The public-domain presets are pooh, eeyore and tigger.
